title: Normalized strict cone representatives for integral pullback
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E/Q_ell, separated finite-type schemes X,Y over a positive-characteristic field k of characteristic different from ell, and g:X -> Y, with the coefficient datum, strict towers T,U,V and coefficient restriction of [def-sfb-integral-pullback-strict-roos-data]. There exist ordinary comparison isomorphisms d, a:T~U and e:restriction(T)~V, chain maps alphaT,alphaU,alphaV to their strict Roos cones, scalar cone isomorphisms epsilon, and natural Roos-to-derived-limit isomorphisms kappaR,kappaC with ordinary-limit inclusions jR,jC. They satisfy the ordinary generator normalization of d and a; e at each level is d followed by inverse ordinaryRho; each alpha has coordinates (0,b) for its actual quotient augmentation; epsilon is diagonal product(e) with the restriction/product comparison and is natural; restriction(alphaT) epsilon = d alphaV. The ordinary inclusions have coordinates (0,z) and localize through kappa to the universal derived-limit comparison. All complexes are arbitrary and unbounded; the R and C module categories remain distinct. The eleven witnesses are fields of the generic product record RoosChainWitness, which carries no new mathematical condition.

proof.text: Use augmentedQuotientTowers to obtain d and a and define e as its theta. Its levelwise formula is d followed by inverse beta; the strict augmentation identities hold on tensor generators and therefore as module maps.

Apply roosAugment to each compatible strict quotient augmentation. The signed cone formula gives coordinates (0,b). Apply augmentedScalarRoosResolution to restriction along C_X -> R_X; compose its cone comparison with Roos(e). Its product and augmentation formulas give IsENormalized and the scalar augmentation equation.

Use exact countable products and the normalized strict Roos comparison over each coefficient ring. The ordinary compatible-family inclusion has zero shifted coordinate, and localization followed by kappa is the universal total right derived limit comparison.

theorem integralRoosChainRepresentatives
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ l)]
    [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [g.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] :
    ∃ w : RoosChainWitness
      (pullR l E g ⋙ res l E X ≅ res l E Y ⋙ pullC l E g)
      (T l E g ≅ U l E g) (T l E g ⋙ towerRes l E X ≅ V l E g)
      (alphaTType l E g) (alphaUType l E g) (alphaVType l E g) (EType l E g)
      (kappaType X (R l E X)) (inclusionType X (R l E X))
      (kappaType X (C l E X)) (inclusionType X (C l E X)),
      PulledReduction.IsOrdinaryNormalized (datum l E) g w.d.inv ∧
      IsLambdaNormalized l E g w.a ∧
      (∀ (M : ModR l E Y) (n : ℕ), (w.e.hom.app M).app (op n) =
        w.d.hom.app (((redR l E Y).obj M).obj (op n)) ≫
          (pullC l E g).map
            (((OrderedExchange.ordinaryRho (datum l E) Y).inv.app M).app (op n))) ∧
      IsAugmentationNormalized l E g w.αT w.αU w.αV ∧
      IsENormalized l E g w.e w.ε ∧
      (∀ P : complexesR l E Y,
        (cxRes l E X).map (w.αT P) ≫ (w.ε P).hom =
          (dComplex l E g w.d).hom.app P ≫ w.αV P) ∧
      IsUnitNormalized X (R l E X) w.κR w.jR ∧ IsUnitNormalized X (C l E X) w.κC w.jC
